title: Breit--Wheeler pair production (categorical)
html:
Definition (Breit--Wheeler pair production).

The Breit--Wheeler process models categorical pair production, \gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+. The fusion of two photons into an electron--positron pair corresponds to an identity in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q):

  \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2
  = 
  \mathrm{NF}(e^-) + \mathrm{NF}(e^+)
  +  \text{binding energy}.

Braid words represent the photon, electron, and positron:

  \gamma = \sigma_0, \qquad
  e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0  \text{ (trefoil)}, \qquad
  e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}  \text{ (mirror trefoil)}.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The underlying categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. We specialise only their archimedean realisation.
